name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
visual_anchor: A big olive-green Tyrannosaurus rex with a few fluffy feathers on its back, standing tall in a sunny valley of ferns and palm trees with a curious, friendly look, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge meat-eating dinosaur that walked on two strong legs
Had very short arms with only two fingers on each hand
Had one of the strongest bites of any land animal ever
Lived in western North America at the very end of the dinosaur age

facts_and_myths.claim: T. rex had only two fingers on each hand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its small arms ended in two clawed fingers, and the arms were surprisingly strong for their size.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: One of the most complete T. rex skeletons, nicknamed Sue, is on display at Chicago's Field Museum.

facts_and_myths.claim: T. rex could only see things that were moving.
facts_and_myths.explanation: That idea comes from movies. Its forward-facing eyes gave it good depth vision, so it could likely see still things well.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its biggest teeth, roots included, were about as long as a banana.

name: Triceratops
visual_anchor: A sturdy orange-brown Triceratops with three shiny horns and a wide patterned frill, munching leafy plants beside a calm river at golden hour, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big plant-eating dinosaur that walked on four legs
Had three horns on its face
Had a large bony frill behind its head
Lived in the same time and place as T. rex

facts_and_myths.claim: The name Triceratops means three-horned face.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It had two long horns above its eyes and one shorter horn on its nose.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Triceratops had a beak like a parrot's for snipping tough plants.

facts_and_myths.claim: Triceratops and Stegosaurus lived at the same time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stegosaurus lived about 80 million years earlier. Triceratops actually lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus!
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A Triceratops skull could be over two meters long, one of the biggest skulls of any land animal.

name: Stegosaurus
visual_anchor: A friendly green Stegosaurus with two rows of tall orange plates along its back and a spiky tail, walking through a sunny Jurassic forest of ferns, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Plant-eating dinosaur that walked on four legs
Had two rows of tall, flat plates along its back
Had four long spikes at the end of its tail
Had a tiny head for its big body and lived in the Jurassic

facts_and_myths.claim: Stegosaurus lived long before T. rex existed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago, roughly 80 million years before T. rex appeared.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Stegosaurus is the official state dinosaur of Colorado.

facts_and_myths.claim: Stegosaurus had a second brain in its hips.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This old idea came from a space in its hip bones. Scientists now agree it was not a brain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its spiky tail is nicknamed the thagomizer, a word that started in a newspaper cartoon.

name: Velociraptor
visual_anchor: A small turkey-sized Velociraptor covered in brown and cream feathers, standing alert on a sandy desert dune under a bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, fast dinosaur that ran on two legs
Was covered in feathers and was about the size of a turkey
Had a big curved claw on each foot
Lived in the deserts of what is now Mongolia

facts_and_myths.claim: Velociraptor had feathers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its arm bones have small bumps called quill knobs, where large feathers were attached.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Velociraptor means swift seizer.

facts_and_myths.claim: Velociraptor was as tall as a grown-up person.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Movies made it look huge, but the real Velociraptor was only about the size of a turkey.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The movie raptors were based more on a bigger cousin called Deinonychus.

name: Brachiosaurus
visual_anchor: A gentle giant Brachiosaurus with a long neck stretching up to nibble leaves from a tall tree, soft morning light over a green valley, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant plant-eating dinosaur with a very long neck
Held its head high like a giraffe to reach treetops
Its front legs were longer than its back legs
Lived in North America during the Late Jurassic

facts_and_myths.claim: Brachiosaurus had front legs longer than its back legs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means arm lizard because of its long front legs, which tilted its body upward.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A close relative mounted in a Berlin museum is one of the tallest dinosaur skeletons on display.

facts_and_myths.claim: Brachiosaurus lived in lakes to hold up its heavy body.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists once thought so, but its strong legs show it walked on land like other long-necked dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Brachiosaurus could reach leaves far higher than a giraffe can.

name: Ankylosaurus
visual_anchor: A low, wide Ankylosaurus covered in bumpy tan armor plates with a round club on its tail, strolling across a flowery meadow on a sunny day, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Low, wide plant-eating dinosaur that walked on four legs
Its back was covered in thick bony armor
Had a heavy bony club at the end of its tail
Lived in North America at the end of the Cretaceous

facts_and_myths.claim: Ankylosaurus had a bony club at the end of its tail.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The heavy club was made of joined bones and could be swung to protect itself.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its name means fused lizard because many of its bones were joined together.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ankylosaurus was one of the biggest dinosaurs of all.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was roughly six to eight meters long, much smaller than the giant long-necked dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ankylosaurus is often called a living tank because of its thick armor.

name: Spinosaurus
visual_anchor: A long Spinosaurus with a tall red-and-orange sail on its back, wading in a shallow sparkling river with a fish nearby, lush green riverbanks, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge meat-eating dinosaur with a tall sail on its back
Had a long, narrow snout like a crocodile
Caught lots of fish in rivers
Lived in North Africa

facts_and_myths.claim: Spinosaurus ate a lot of fish.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its long, narrow jaws and cone-shaped teeth were great for grabbing slippery fish, like a crocodile's.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spinosaurus may have been longer than T. rex, making it one of the longest meat-eating dinosaurs.

facts_and_myths.claim: Spinosaurus and T. rex lived at the same time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spinosaurus lived in Africa millions of years earlier, so the two never met outside of movies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its sail was held up by very long spines growing from its backbone.

name: Diplodocus
visual_anchor: A very long gray-green Diplodocus with a long neck and whip-like tail, stretched across a wide sunny plain with ferns and distant hills, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge plant-eating dinosaur with a long neck
Had an extra-long, whip-like tail
Had peg-shaped teeth for stripping leaves off branches
Lived in North America during the Late Jurassic

facts_and_myths.claim: Copies of one Diplodocus skeleton stand in museums around the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Businessman Andrew Carnegie gave casts of a skeleton nicknamed Dippy to museums in many countries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A Dippy cast welcomed visitors at London's Natural History Museum for over 100 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Diplodocus was the heaviest dinosaur ever.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was very long but quite slim. Giants like Argentinosaurus were much heavier.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some scientists think Diplodocus could flick its tail tip faster than the speed of sound.

name: Parasaurolophus
visual_anchor: A cheerful duck-billed Parasaurolophus with a long curved tube-shaped crest, calling out beside a misty lake surrounded by tall green trees, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Duck-billed plant-eating dinosaur
Had a long, hollow crest curving back from its head
May have used its crest to make loud honking calls
Lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous

facts_and_myths.claim: Parasaurolophus could probably make deep sounds with its crest.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Air tubes ran through its hollow crest like a trombone, so it likely made booming calls.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists used computer models of its crest to recreate what its call may have sounded like.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Parasaurolophus crest was a snorkel for breathing underwater.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists dropped this idea because the crest had no opening at the top.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Parasaurolophus could walk on two legs or on all four.

name: Pachycephalosaurus
visual_anchor: A Pachycephalosaurus with a smooth round dome on its head ringed by little knobs, standing on two legs in a sunny grassy clearing, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Plant-eating dinosaur that walked on two legs
Had a very thick, dome-shaped skull
Small knobs and short spikes ringed the dome
Lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous

facts_and_myths.claim: Pachycephalosaurus had a very thick skull roof.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means thick-headed lizard. The bony dome on top could be about 25 centimeters thick.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some scientists think Dracorex and Stygimoloch were just young Pachycephalosaurus.

facts_and_myths.claim: Scientists are certain Pachycephalosaurus smashed heads together like rams.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists still debate it. Some think they pushed sides instead, or used their domes for showing off.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its dome was ringed by little bony knobs and short spikes.

name: Allosaurus
visual_anchor: A sleek brown-and-gold Allosaurus with small ridges above its eyes, standing on two legs among tall Jurassic conifers on a bright day, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large meat-eating dinosaur that walked on two legs
Had small ridges like little horns above its eyes
Had three fingers with big curved claws on each hand
Was a top hunter in Jurassic North America

facts_and_myths.claim: Allosaurus lived millions of years before T. rex.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Allosaurus lived about 150 million years ago, in the Jurassic, at the same time as Stegosaurus.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A famous Allosaurus skeleton nicknamed Big Al was found in Wyoming.

facts_and_myths.claim: Allosaurus had just two fingers on each hand like T. rex.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Allosaurus had three fingers on each hand, each with a big curved claw.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Allosaurus is the official state fossil of Utah.

name: Iguanodon
visual_anchor: A large green Iguanodon with a pointed thumb spike, reaching for leafy branches in a sunny Cretaceous forest, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large plant-eating dinosaur that could walk on two or four legs
Had a cone-shaped spike on each thumb
Was one of the very first dinosaurs ever given a name
Many fossils were found in England and Belgium

facts_and_myths.claim: Iguanodon had a spike on each thumb.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The cone-shaped thumb spike may have helped it protect itself or grab food.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Iguanodon was only the second dinosaur ever to get a scientific name, back in 1825.

facts_and_myths.claim: Iguanodon had a horn on its nose.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early scientists put the thumb spike on its nose. Later skeletons showed it belonged on the hand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dozens of Iguanodon skeletons were found together deep in a coal mine in Belgium.

name: Archaeopteryx
visual_anchor: A crow-sized Archaeopteryx with black-and-brown feathered wings and a long feathery tail, perched on a branch above a sunny lagoon, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Crow-sized animal with feathers and wings
Had teeth in its jaws and a long bony tail
Fossils were found in limestone in Germany
Famous as an early link between dinosaurs and birds

facts_and_myths.claim: Archaeopteryx had teeth and a bony tail, unlike birds today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It mixed bird features like feathered wings with dinosaur features like teeth, claws and a long tail.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its fossils formed in fine limestone that kept even the outlines of its feathers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Archaeopteryx is the direct ancestor of all birds today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists see it as an early bird relative, not the exact great-grandparent of today's birds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Archaeopteryx was first described in 1861, just two years after Darwin's famous book on evolution.

name: Carnotaurus
visual_anchor: A reddish Carnotaurus with two short bull-like horns above its eyes and tiny arms, standing on a dusty plain under a wide orange sunset sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Meat-eating dinosaur that walked on two legs
Had two thick horns above its eyes, like a bull
Had extremely tiny arms, even for a big meat-eater
Lived in what is now Argentina

facts_and_myths.claim: Carnotaurus had two horns above its eyes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means meat-eating bull because of those short, thick horns.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists found impressions of its skin, showing rows of bumpy scales.

facts_and_myths.claim: Carnotaurus lived alongside T. rex in North America.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Carnotaurus lived in South America, in what is now Argentina, so it never met T. rex.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: For its body size, Carnotaurus had some of the tiniest arms of any big meat-eating dinosaur.

name: Apatosaurus
visual_anchor: A huge gentle Apatosaurus with a thick neck and long tail held up off the ground, walking beside a shining lake under fluffy white clouds, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant plant-eating dinosaur with a long neck
Its neck was unusually thick and heavy
Lived in North America during the Late Jurassic
Was famously mixed up with a dinosaur called Brontosaurus

facts_and_myths.claim: Apatosaurus was once mixed up with Brontosaurus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists once merged them under the name Apatosaurus. A 2015 study argued Brontosaurus is separate after all.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Apatosaurus means deceptive lizard.

facts_and_myths.claim: Long-necked dinosaurs like Apatosaurus dragged their tails on the ground.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fossil footprint trails rarely show tail marks, so scientists think they held their tails up.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Old museum skeletons were later rebuilt to lift their tails off the floor.

name: Argentinosaurus
visual_anchor: An enormous long-necked Argentinosaurus towering over small trees on a wide green plain, with a flock of little birds flying past its neck for scale, bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Gigantic long-necked plant-eating dinosaur
One of the largest land animals ever found
Belonged to a giant dinosaur group called titanosaurs
Named after the South American country where it was found

facts_and_myths.claim: Argentinosaurus is one of the largest land animals ever found.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists estimate it was over 30 meters long, based on a few giant bones.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Just one of its backbones is about as tall as a grown-up person.

facts_and_myths.claim: Scientists have found a complete Argentinosaurus skeleton.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only a few bones have been found, so its size is estimated by comparing it with relatives.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This plant-eater may have weighed about as much as ten big elephants.

name: Oviraptor
visual_anchor: A feathered Oviraptor with a short crested head and toothless beak, sitting gently on a nest of oval eggs in a sandy desert, warm sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small feathered dinosaur that walked on two legs
Had a short, toothless beak and a crest on its head
Lived in the deserts of what is now Mongolia
Its name means egg thief, but that turned out to be unfair

facts_and_myths.claim: Oviraptor had a beak and no teeth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its short, strong beak was toothless, and scientists still debate exactly what it ate.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some Oviraptor relatives were found sitting on nests with arms spread, like a bird keeping eggs warm.

facts_and_myths.claim: Oviraptor stole and ate other dinosaurs' eggs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means egg thief, but the eggs found with it turned out to be its own kind.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Oviraptor was a caring parent that likely guarded its nest like birds do today.

name: Gallimimus
visual_anchor: A slender ostrich-like Gallimimus with long legs and a small beaked head, running across a golden grassy plain with dust swirling behind it, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Fast dinosaur shaped a lot like an ostrich
Had long legs built for running
Had a small head with a toothless beak
Lived in what is now Mongolia

facts_and_myths.claim: The name Gallimimus means chicken mimic.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists thought parts of its neck looked like a chicken's, so they named it after one.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A herd of Gallimimus raced across the screen in the first Jurassic Park movie.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gallimimus had big sharp teeth for catching large animals.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It had a toothless beak and likely ate plants, insects and small animals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: With legs like an ostrich, it was probably one of the fastest dinosaurs.

name: Therizinosaurus
visual_anchor: A tall, fluffy-feathered Therizinosaurus with enormous curved hand claws, gently pulling down a leafy branch in a green forest, soft daylight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tall, pot-bellied dinosaur that was probably feathered
Had enormous curved claws on its hands
Probably ate plants instead of meat
Lived in what is now Mongolia

facts_and_myths.claim: Therizinosaurus had some of the longest claws of any land animal.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its hand claws could reach about one meter long, as long as a baseball bat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its name means scythe lizard, because its claws curve like a farmer's cutting blade.

facts_and_myths.claim: Therizinosaurus used its giant claws to hunt other dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists think it mostly ate plants and used its claws to pull branches closer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When its claws were first found, scientists thought they came from a giant turtle-like reptile.

name: Microraptor
visual_anchor: A small crow-sized Microraptor with glossy black shimmering feathers on its arms and legs, gliding between leafy trees in a bright forest, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small feathered dinosaur about the size of a crow
Had feathered wings on both its arms and its legs
Probably glided or flew between trees
Fossils were found in China

facts_and_myths.claim: Microraptor had feathered wings on its arms and legs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Long feathers on all four limbs helped it glide, and maybe fly, between trees.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists studying its fossil feathers found they were glossy black with a shimmer, like a starling.

facts_and_myths.claim: No dinosaurs had feathers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fossils like Microraptor from China clearly show feathers, and many other dinosaurs had them too.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: One Microraptor fossil was found with the remains of a small fish in its belly.

name: Protoceratops
visual_anchor: A sheep-sized Protoceratops with a parrot-like beak and a neat neck frill, resting on red sandstone in a sunny desert, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small plant-eating dinosaur about the size of a sheep
Had a parrot-like beak and a frill on its neck
Was an early cousin of Triceratops without big horns
Many skeletons were found in the Gobi Desert

facts_and_myths.claim: Protoceratops was about the size of a sheep.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This small frilled dinosaur was much smaller than its famous cousin Triceratops.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some historians think Protoceratops fossils inspired ancient legends of the griffin.

facts_and_myths.claim: Protoceratops had three big horns like Triceratops.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It had a neck frill and a beak, but no big horns, just a small bump on its nose.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists have found many Protoceratops skeletons, from tiny babies to adults.

name: Edmontosaurus
visual_anchor: A large duck-billed Edmontosaurus with a flat head and wide beak, grazing on low plants near a cool northern forest on a sunny day, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large duck-billed plant-eating dinosaur
Had a flat head with no big bony crest
Had hundreds of teeth packed together for grinding plants
Named after rocks near a city in Canada

facts_and_myths.claim: Edmontosaurus had hundreds of teeth in its jaws.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rows of teeth ground tough plants, and new teeth kept replacing worn ones.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some Edmontosaurus fossils are mummies that kept the shape of their scaly skin.

facts_and_myths.claim: Edmontosaurus had a tall bony crest like Parasaurolophus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its head was flat, though one fossil showed a soft, fleshy comb like a rooster's.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was named after rocks near Edmonton, a city in Canada.

name: Pteranodon
visual_anchor: A Pteranodon with wide leathery wings and a long backward-pointing crest, soaring over a sparkling blue sea with white waves below, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Flying reptile with big wings made of skin
Had a long crest pointing back from its head
Had a long beak with no teeth
Caught fish over an ancient sea that covered Kansas

facts_and_myths.claim: Pteranodon had no teeth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means wing without tooth. It likely scooped up fish with its long beak.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Big adults had wings over six meters across, wider than a giraffe is tall.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pteranodon was a flying dinosaur.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was a pterosaur, a flying reptile. Pterosaurs were close cousins of dinosaurs, not dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pterosaurs were the first animals with backbones to fly by flapping their wings.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
visual_anchor: A giant Quetzalcoatlus standing tall as a giraffe on a grassy plain with wings folded, its long beak pointing down at the grass, golden evening light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge flying reptile with a very long beak and neck
One of the largest flying animals ever
Standing on the ground, it was about as tall as a giraffe
Fossils were found in Texas

facts_and_myths.claim: Quetzalcoatlus was one of the largest flying animals ever.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its wingspan was around 10 to 11 meters, about as wide as a small airplane.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was named after Quetzalcoatl, a feathered serpent from Aztec legends.

facts_and_myths.claim: Quetzalcoatlus only fed by catching fish over the ocean.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists think it often walked on land, picking up small animals like a giant stork.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It walked on all four limbs, folding its wings up when on the ground.

name: Mosasaurus
visual_anchor: A long blue-gray Mosasaurus with paddle flippers and a finned tail, gliding through clear turquoise ocean water with sunbeams shining down, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Huge reptile that lived in the sea
Had paddle-like flippers and a long, finned tail
Was related to today's lizards and snakes
Its first fossil was found near the Meuse River in Europe

facts_and_myths.claim: Mosasaurus was a giant sea reptile, not a dinosaur.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mosasaurs were ocean-going reptiles related to today's lizards and snakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its name means lizard of the Meuse, a river in the Netherlands where it was found.

facts_and_myths.claim: The real Mosasaurus was as huge as the one in Jurassic World.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The movie made it much bigger. Real ones were roughly as long as a bus.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It had an extra row of teeth on the roof of its mouth to grip slippery food.

name: Plesiosaurus
visual_anchor: A Plesiosaurus with a long neck, small head and four big flippers, swimming gracefully through a sunlit green-blue sea full of tiny fish, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sea reptile with a long neck and a small head
Swam using four large flippers
Lived in the seas of the Early Jurassic
A famous early skeleton was found by Mary Anning in England

facts_and_myths.claim: Plesiosaurus swam using four big flippers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It moved with four paddle-shaped limbs, a bit like a sea turtle flying underwater.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fossil hunter Mary Anning found an early complete Plesiosaurus skeleton in England in 1823.

facts_and_myths.claim: Plesiosaurus was a swimming dinosaur.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was a marine reptile from a separate group that lived at the same time as dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many drawings of the Loch Ness Monster legend look a lot like a plesiosaur.

name: Ichthyosaurus
visual_anchor: A sleek dolphin-shaped Ichthyosaurus with big round eyes and a tall tail fin, leaping through bright blue waves under a sunny sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sea reptile shaped a lot like a dolphin
Had very large eyes and a tall tail fin
Gave birth to live babies instead of laying eggs
Early fossils were found by Mary Anning and her brother in England

facts_and_myths.claim: Ichthyosaurs gave birth to live babies in the water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fossils show mothers with babies, so they did not need to lay eggs on beaches.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mary Anning and her brother found one of the first ichthyosaur fossils in England.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ichthyosaurus was an early kind of dolphin.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It looked like a dolphin but was a reptile. Dolphins are mammals that appeared much later.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some ichthyosaurs had eyes about as big as dinner plates.

name: Dimorphodon
visual_anchor: A colorful Dimorphodon with an oversized puffin-like head, small wings and a long tail, perched on a rocky seaside cliff on a sunny morning, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small flying reptile with an oversized head
Had a long tail behind its wings
Had two different kinds of teeth
Lived in Early Jurassic England

facts_and_myths.claim: Dimorphodon had two different kinds of teeth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its name means two-form tooth: long teeth at the front and small teeth behind.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its first fossil was found by Mary Anning on the coast of England.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dimorphodon's big head was too heavy for it to fly.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its large skull had big openings that kept it light enough for flight.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It had a long tail, unlike Pteranodon, which had a very short one.

name: Elasmosaurus
visual_anchor: An Elasmosaurus with an extremely long neck stretched straight out and four flippers, swimming calmly through a clear blue sea with sunlight rippling above, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sea reptile with an extremely long neck
Had a small head and four flippers
Its neck had about 72 bones
Lived in a sea that once covered Kansas

facts_and_myths.claim: Elasmosaurus had about 72 bones in its neck.
facts_and_myths.explanation: That is more than almost any other animal. Its neck was over half its body length.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Giraffes have only seven neck bones, even though their necks look very long.

facts_and_myths.claim: Elasmosaurus held its neck high above the water like a swan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its long neck was stiff and heavy, so scientists think it mostly held it straight out.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A famous scientist once put its head on the wrong end, on the tip of its tail!

name: Liopleurodon
visual_anchor: A big-headed Liopleurodon with a short neck and four strong flippers, swimming through deep blue water with shafts of sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sea reptile with a short neck and a very large head
Swam with four strong flippers
Was a top hunter in Jurassic seas
Fossils come from England and France

facts_and_myths.claim: Liopleurodon had a short neck and a very large head.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was a pliosaur, a short-necked cousin of the long-necked plesiosaurs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its long jaws were lined with big, cone-shaped teeth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Liopleurodon was 25 meters long, as a famous TV show claimed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists now think adults were more like six or seven meters long.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Liopleurodon lived in the Jurassic, millions of years before Mosasaurus appeared.

name: Woolly Mammoth
visual_anchor: A shaggy brown woolly mammoth with long curved tusks, walking through a snowy meadow with snowflakes falling and pale blue mountains behind, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large elephant relative covered in shaggy fur
Had very long, curved tusks
Had small ears and a short tail to keep in heat
Lived in cold lands during the Ice Age

facts_and_myths.claim: Some woolly mammoths were still around when Egypt's pyramids were built.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A small group lived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic until about 4,000 years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mammoth tusks could grow about four meters long.

facts_and_myths.claim: Woolly mammoths were much bigger than today's elephants.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most woolly mammoths were about the size of an African elephant.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their small ears and short tails helped stop heat from escaping in the cold.

name: Saber-Toothed Cat
visual_anchor: A sturdy tan saber-toothed cat with two long upper fangs and a short tail, resting on a rocky ledge above a grassy Ice Age valley in warm sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big Ice Age cat with two very long upper teeth
Had a short tail and powerful front legs
Lived in North and South America
Thousands of its fossils were found in tar pits in Los Angeles

facts_and_myths.claim: Smilodon could open its jaws extremely wide.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its mouth opened about 120 degrees, making room to use its long upper teeth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Smilodon is the official state fossil of California.

facts_and_myths.claim: The saber-toothed cat was a kind of tiger.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite the nickname, Smilodon was not closely related to tigers or other living big cats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thousands of Smilodon fossils have been found at the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles.

name: Megalodon
visual_anchor: A gigantic gray megalodon shark gliding through bright blue ocean water beside a small school of silver fish for scale, sunbeams from above, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant prehistoric shark
Much bigger than a great white shark
Had huge triangular teeth with jagged edges
Disappeared from the oceans millions of years ago

facts_and_myths.claim: Megalodon teeth could be about as big as a grown-up's hand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The largest megalodon teeth are over 15 centimeters long. Its name means big tooth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Megalodon fossils are mostly teeth, because shark skeletons are made of soft cartilage.

facts_and_myths.claim: Megalodon still lives hidden in the deep ocean.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Megalodon vanished millions of years ago, and no living one has ever been found.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sharks replace their teeth all their lives, so one megalodon could leave thousands behind.

name: Woolly Rhinoceros
visual_anchor: A shaggy reddish-brown woolly rhinoceros with a long curved front horn, grazing on frosty grass across a wide snowy plain, soft winter sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Rhino covered in thick shaggy fur
Had a very long, flattened front horn
Grazed on cold grasslands across Europe and Asia
Was painted by ancient people on cave walls in France

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient people painted woolly rhinos on cave walls.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Woolly rhinos appear in cave art in France, including the famous Chauvet Cave.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its long front horn may have helped it sweep snow aside to reach grass.

facts_and_myths.claim: Woolly rhinos were close relatives of woolly mammoths.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Both had shaggy fur and lived in the cold, but rhinos and mammoths are very different animal families.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its closest living relative is the Sumatran rhino, the hairiest rhino today.

name: Giant Ground Sloth
visual_anchor: A huge shaggy giant ground sloth standing on its back legs to pull down a leafy branch with its big claws, sunny South American woodland, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Enormous furry plant-eater with big curved claws
Lived on the ground instead of in trees
Could stand on its back legs to reach leaves
Lived in South America during the Ice Age

facts_and_myths.claim: Megatherium was about as big as an elephant.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This giant ground sloth could weigh several tonnes and stand tall on its back legs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Charles Darwin collected giant ground sloth fossils during his famous voyage on the HMS Beagle.

facts_and_myths.claim: Giant ground sloths hung upside down from trees like sloths today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were far too heavy. They lived on the ground and stood up to reach leaves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because of its big claws, it walked on the sides of its feet.

name: Dodo
visual_anchor: A plump gray dodo with a big hooked yellow-green beak and a tuft of tail feathers, standing on a sunny tropical beach with palm trees, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large bird that could not fly
Had a big, hooked beak
Lived only on the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean
Disappeared in the 1600s after sailors arrived

facts_and_myths.claim: The dodo was a flightless bird from the island of Mauritius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With no big predators on the island, it lived on the ground and did not need to fly.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The dodo's closest living relative is the colorful Nicobar pigeon.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dodos were fat, clumsy, slow birds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Old paintings showed overfed birds kept by people. Scientists think wild dodos were slimmer and quite active.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A dodo appears as a character in the book Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

name: Trilobite
visual_anchor: A group of colorful trilobites with segmented shells crawling across a sandy sea floor among swaying seaweed, soft blue underwater light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small sea creature with a hard, segmented shell
Its body was divided into three long sections
Distant relative of crabs and insects
Lived in the oceans long before the first dinosaurs

facts_and_myths.claim: Trilobites had eyes with lenses made of a clear mineral.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their eye lenses were made of calcite, a mineral, which is why their eyes fossilized so well.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Trilobites lived in the oceans for more than 250 million years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Trilobites lived at the same time as T. rex.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Trilobites disappeared about 252 million years ago, long before the first dinosaurs appeared.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some trilobites could roll up into a ball, like a pill bug.

name: Ammonite
visual_anchor: A shiny ammonite with a coiled striped spiral shell and little tentacles, floating in clear turquoise water above a sandy sea floor, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sea animal that lived inside a coiled, spiral shell
Was related to squid and octopuses
Its shell had chambers that helped it float
Disappeared at about the same time as the dinosaurs

facts_and_myths.claim: Ammonites were related to octopuses and squid.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were mollusks with tentacles that lived in coiled, chambered shells, like today's nautilus.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some ammonite shells grew nearly two meters across.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ammonite fossils are curled-up snakes that turned to stone.
facts_and_myths.explanation: People once carved snake heads onto them, but ammonites were sea animals with shells.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ammonites are so common that scientists use them to tell the age of rocks.

name: Dire Wolf
visual_anchor: A sturdy light-gray dire wolf with a broad head standing on a grassy hill at sunrise, its fur glowing in the warm light, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large wolf-like Ice Age animal
Was a bit bigger and heavier than most gray wolves
Lived across North and South America
Thousands of its fossils were found in tar pits in Los Angeles

facts_and_myths.claim: Dire wolves were bigger and heavier than most gray wolves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were a bit larger than gray wolves, with strong jaws for crunching bones.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thousands of dire wolf fossils have been found at the La Brea Tar Pits.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dire wolves were the ancestors of today's gray wolves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: DNA shows dire wolves were a separate branch of dog relatives that split off millions of years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dire wolves lived in the Americas until around 13,000 years ago.

name: Glyptodon
visual_anchor: A big round Glyptodon with a domed shell made of many small patterned plates, walking across a grassy South American plain under a bright sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large mammal with a huge, domed shell
Its shell was made of many small bony plates
Was a giant relative of armadillos
Lived in South America during the Ice Age

facts_and_myths.claim: Glyptodon was a giant relative of armadillos.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It had a huge domed shell made of many small bony plates joined together.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its shell was roughly the size of a small car.

facts_and_myths.claim: Glyptodon was a giant turtle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It looked a bit like a turtle, but it was a mammal, closely related to armadillos.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some scientists think early people in South America may have used glyptodon shells as shelters.
